title: Merge Intervals
prompt:
Given an array of `intervals` (in any order), merge all overlapping intervals and return the non-overlapping result sorted by start. Intervals that touch at an endpoint overlap.

**Example**: `[[1,3],[2,6],[8,10],[15,18]]` → `[[1,6],[8,10],[15,18]]`.

**Constraints**: `1 ≤ intervals.length ≤ 10^4`.

tests.note: fully contained — don't shrink the end!

hints: If the intervals were in start order, which already-merged interval could the next one possibly overlap?
Only the last one you merged. Sort by start (with `Integer.compare`) and sweep, comparing each interval to the last merged one.
Overlap iff `cur[0] <= last[1]`. Then `last[1] = Math.max(last[1], cur[1])`. The max handles a contained interval like [2,3] inside [1,4].

solution.explanation: After sorting by start, an interval can only overlap the most recent merged group, because earlier groups ended before that group began. So one comparison decides whether to extend or append. O(n log n) time for the sort, O(n) space for the output.
